clue: Head Office would like a festive photo of the team enjoying the tin. Deadline: 20 December.
The tin: round, tartan, about the size of a dinner plate, labelled Assorted Shortbread. Last seen in the spring.
note: Distinctive. Should be easy to spot.

clue: Santa: known biscuit thief, enters homes uninvited once a year, has never been charged.
Santa’s sack has never been searched by any authority.
note: Obtain a warrant. Find out who issues warrants.

clue: The reindeer says Santa does not touch biscuits until 24 December, “for union reasons”.
The reindeer asked to be paid in carrots.
A shortbread crumb (not mince pie) found in the spare room museum, now hanging on the Christmas tree.
note: Proof the tin passed through. Or an old crumb. Tastes recent.

clue: Areas searched: loft, garage, under the tree, behind the sofa, inside the turkey. Not searched: the desk.
note: No need. The desk is where the work happens.

clue: Last year’s Secret Santa present, still wrapped, from “???”.
Asked to point, the shortbread finger pointed at the study, the kitchen, the tree and about forty other things.
Santa’s Christmas card was returned: “Not known at this address.”
note: Exactly what a guilty man would say.

clue: A circular mark on the editor’s desk, 19cm across. The tin is 19cm across.
note: Coincidence. Ruled out: advent candle (square), Christmas pudding (eaten, 2024).

clue: The robin appears on most Christmas cards ever printed. It is always watching.
A client says the editor was “sitting very tall today”.
The mince pie left as bait was eaten. So was the milk.
note: By me, for realism. Does not count.

clue: A faint rattle can be heard when the editor types quickly.
The suspect sketch, with the beard, hat and sack removed as disguises, shows a man in a Christmas jumper, from the chest up, looking pleased with himself.
note: Very typical face. Could be anyone.

clue: The Christmas tree has been dropping needles all week.
The houseplant was moved six inches during the spring clean, to make room for something.
note: Plant cleared. Whatever it was, irrelevant.

clue: Anonymous letter: “Have you tried looking under things?”
note: Looked under everything that is a thing. Tools are not things.

clue: The kitchen speaker hears a rattle from the study every time an angry email is typed: 41 times this week.
With bass-heavy festive music on, something on the desk buzzes like a very small metal drum.
Expense claim, March: “office furniture (tartan), £0.00. Found it in the house, bargain.”
Customs: the only tartan item seen this year is at the bottom of the editor’s own video calls.
note: Lots of people have tartan. Tinsel applied.

clue: Team email, March: a photograph captioned “my new tartan stand — game changer”.
The crossword answers are TIN, UNDER, LAPTOP, TARTAN, MARCH and YOU, filled in overnight in the editor’s handwriting.
Handover note from Cebu and Sydney: “Lift the laptop.”
note: Great motto for the new year. Mug ordered.

clue: On video the editor is noticeably taller than in person. Tilting the camera down shows a flash of tartan.
There are no biscuits anywhere in the house.
Packing list: “3. Laptop. 4. Find out why laptop is so heavy.”
The tin, recovered from under the laptop. Contents: Assorted Shortbread, nine months old, one finger short.
